SPLIT into 5 children: 3 reused accepted declarations with byte-identical frozen types (no new DAG node) and 2 new nodes.

Why split.
- The supplied proof has two independent halves with different arguments. (i) Upper bound M_W(T) ≤ I(W): step 1(1a) and step 2, a pointwise duality bound plus domination. (ii) Lower bound I(W) ≤ M_W(T) when I(W) < ∞: steps 1 and 3, Lusin, Tietze/normalization/mollification/cut-off and an integral estimate. The selected conclusion is exactly (i) together with (ii) + antisymmetry.
- Steps (3b)–(3e) are precisely two accepted declarations of the imrep_mass_and_support branch: dor_ims_lusin_continuousOn (Lusin for Λ^k-valued maps; the pinned Mathlib has only Lusin separation and Lusin–Souslin, no Lusin continuity theorem) and dor_ims_smooth_unit_approx (Tietze, retraction to |·| ≤ 1, cut-off, mollification, packaged as a δ-approximation on K). The split makes them listed prerequisites of the lower-bound child.
- The accepted mass lemmas dor_ims_massOn_le_measure / dor_ims_measure_le_massOn concern IMRep only (ℕ-valued multiplicity, rectifiable carrier, representation on all of 𝒟^k(U)); they do not apply to a real weight θ' represented only on forms supported in V.

subproblems.title: Euclidean coefficient-norm duality for unit simple n-vectors (Cauchy–Binet)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), ∃ L : MultiVector P n →L[ℝ] Covector (Euclid P) n, ∀ (ξ : MultiVector P n) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q → (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, |ξ α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) ∧ covectorEuclideanNorm (L ξ) ≤ 1 ∧ ξ (L ξ) = 1
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note. This child is the accepted declaration Submission.dor_ims_unitOrientation_dual of DAG node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.imrep_mass_and_support-a1.unit_orientation_duality-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit 9c8432cb0101). It is reused with its identical frozen Lean type, so it adds no DAG node. Used by the new children oriented_mass_upper (part (a): the pointwise bound |ξ'(x)(α)| ≤ |α|) and oriented_mass_lower (parts (a)–(c): the pointwise bound and the continuous dual field L∘ξ' fed to Lusin). The reviewed proof from that node's parent-supplied handoff follows verbatim.

Source: step 1 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, §1: coordinate covectors dx^I and the pairing of Λⁿ with Λₙ). The Cauchy–Binet identity is proved inline.
Notation:
- e_0, …, e_{P−1} is the standard basis of ℝ^P (EuclideanSpace.basisFun), and v(i) is the i-th coordinate of v ∈ ℝ^P.
- Λⁿ := Covector (Euclid P) n, the continuous alternating n-linear maps (ℝ^P)^n → ℝ; Λₙ := MultiVector P n = Λⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝ.
- 𝓘 is the finite set of strictly increasing I : Fin n → Fin P, and e_I := (e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}).
- For α ∈ Λⁿ, |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I ∈ 𝓘} α(e_I)²)^{1/2}. The defining sum runs over all I : Fin n → Fin P, with term α(e_I)² for strictly increasing I and 0 otherwise, so it is the same sum.
- For v = (v_0, …, v_{n−1}) ∈ (ℝ^P)^n and I ∈ 𝓘, v^I is the n×n matrix with (k, j) entry v_j(I(k)).
1. (Coordinate covectors.) For I ∈ 𝓘 let dx^I ∈ Λⁿ be dx^I(v) := det(v^I). It is n-linear and alternating in v, because the determinant is multilinear and alternating in its columns and column j, (v_j(I(k)))_k, depends linearly on v_j. It is continuous because ℝ^P is finite-dimensional. In SimonGMT (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter06.FormsDuality), dx^I = wedgeCovectors n (fun k ↦ EuclideanSpace.proj (I k)), and wedgeCovectors_apply_det gives exactly this formula. For n = 0, dx^I is the constant covector 1, the determinant of the empty matrix.
2. (Kronecker property.) For I, J ∈ 𝓘, dx^I(e_J) = 1 if I = J and dx^I(e_J) = 0 if I ≠ J. The matrix (e_J)^I has (k, j) entry 1 if I(k) = J(j) and 0 otherwise. If I = J it is the identity matrix. If I ≠ J, the ranges differ, because a strictly increasing map Fin n → Fin P is the increasing enumeration of its range. Both ranges have n elements, so some I(k) is not in range J. Row k of (e_J)^I is then zero, and the determinant is 0.
3. (Expansion.) For every α ∈ Λⁿ and v ∈ (ℝ^P)^n: α(v) = Σ_{I ∈ 𝓘} α(e_I)·dx^I(v).
 Both sides are alternating n-linear functions of v; the right side is a linear combination of the dx^I. By multilinearity, two n-linear maps on ℝ^P agree once they agree on every basis tuple e_f := (e_{f(0)}, …, e_{f(n−1)}), f : Fin n → Fin P.
 - If f is not injective, both alternating maps vanish at e_f, which has a repeated entry.
 - If f is injective, let J ∈ 𝓘 enumerate range f increasingly, and let σ be the permutation of Fin n with f = J ∘ σ. By alternation, each side at e_f equals sign(σ) times its value at e_J. At e_J the right side is Σ_I α(e_I) dx^I(e_J) = α(e_J) by step 2.
 Hence the two sides agree.
4. (Sum of squared minors; Cauchy–Binet.) For every orthonormal family τ = (τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) in ℝ^P, Σ_{I ∈ 𝓘} det(τ^I)² = 1. This is the Cauchy–Binet formula det(AᵀA) = Σ_I det(A_I)² for the P×n matrix A with columns τ_j, where AᵀA = Id. Self-contained derivation:
 - Let δ_τ ∈ Λⁿ be δ_τ(v) := det(⟨τ_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j}. It is n-linear, alternating and continuous for the same reasons as dx^I, and equals wedgeCovectors n (fun i ↦ ⟨τ_i, ·⟩).
 - By orthonormality, δ_τ(τ) = det(⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩) = det(Id) = 1.
 - δ_τ(e_I) = det(τ_i(I(j)))_{i,j} = det((τ^I)ᵀ) = det(τ^I), and dx^I(τ) = det(τ^I).
 - Step 3 with α = δ_τ and v = τ gives 1 = δ_τ(τ) = Σ_I δ_τ(e_I)·dx^I(τ) = Σ_I det(τ^I)².
5. (Proof of (a).) Let ξ, Q satisfy IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q, with orthonormal τ and sign s, so ξ(α) = s·α(τ) for all α. For α ∈ Λⁿ, step 3 and the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality in ℝ^𝓘 give
 |ξ(α)| = |α(τ)| = |Σ_I α(e_I) det(τ^I)| ≤ (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2}·(Σ_I det(τ^I)²)^{1/2} = |α|·1,
 using step 4.
6. (Definition of L.) For ζ ∈ Λₙ put L(ζ) := Σ_{I ∈ 𝓘} ζ(dx^I)·dx^I. Each ζ ↦ ζ(dx^I) is evaluation at a fixed point, a continuous linear functional on Λₙ. So L is a finite sum of continuous linear maps Λₙ → Λⁿ, i.e. L ∈ (MultiVector P n →L[ℝ] Covector (Euclid P) n). For example, L = Σ_I (ContinuousLinearMap.apply ℝ ℝ (dx^I)).smulRight (dx^I). L does not depend on ξ.
7. (Coefficients of L(ζ).) For J ∈ 𝓘, step 2 gives L(ζ)(e_J) = Σ_I ζ(dx^I)·dx^I(e_J) = ζ(dx^J). Hence |L(ζ)|² = Σ_{J ∈ 𝓘} ζ(dx^J)².
8. (Proof of (b) and (c).) For ξ as in step 5, ξ(dx^J) = s·dx^J(τ) = s·det(τ^J).
 - By step 7 and step 4, |L(ξ)|² = Σ_J s²·det(τ^J)² = 1, so |L(ξ)| = 1 ≤ 1.
 - By linearity of ξ, ξ(L(ξ)) = Σ_I ξ(dx^I)·ξ(dx^I) = Σ_I det(τ^I)² = 1.
9. (Degenerate cases need no separate treatment.)
 - For n = 0, 𝓘 consists of the empty map, e_∅ is the empty tuple, dx^∅ = 1 and |α| = |α(e_∅)|. Steps 1–8 hold verbatim.
 - If n > P, then 𝓘 = ∅ and step 4 would give 0 = 1. So ℝ^P has no orthonormal family of n vectors, the hypothesis IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q never holds, and the statement is vacuous (L = 0).
proof_key_steps: Define dx^I(v) = det(v_j(I(k)))_{k,j} (SimonGMT wedgeCovectors of coordinate projections); dx^I(e_J) = δ_IJ for strictly increasing I, J.
Expansion α(v) = Σ_I α(e_I)·dx^I(v): both sides are alternating multilinear and agree on all basis tuples.
Σ_I det(τ^I)² = 1 for orthonormal τ (Cauchy–Binet), by expanding δ_τ(v) = det(⟨τ_i, v_j⟩) at v = τ.
Cauchy–Schwarz gives |ξ(α)| = |α(τ)| ≤ |α|.
L(ζ) = Σ_I ζ(dx^I)·dx^I is continuous linear, with |L(ξ)|² = Σ_I det(τ^I)² = 1 and ξ(L(ξ)) = Σ_I det(τ^I)² = 1.

subproblems.title: Lusin's theorem for covector fields on ℝ^P (compact form)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n be natural numbers and μ a measure on ℝ^P (Borel σ-algebra). Let A ⊆ ℝ^P be measurable with μ(A) < ∞, f : ℝ^P → Λⁿ(ℝ^P) (Covector (Euclid P) n) μ-a.e. strongly measurable, and ε > 0 real. Then there is a compact K ⊆ A with μ(A ∖ K) < ε on which f is continuous (ContinuousOn f K).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (A : Set (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n) (ε : ℝ), MeasurableSet A → μ A ≠ ∞ → AEStronglyMeasurable f μ → 0 < ε → ∃ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K ∧ K ⊆ A ∧ μ (A \ K) < ENNReal.ofReal ε ∧ ContinuousOn f K
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note. This child is the accepted declaration Submission.dor_ims_lusin_continuousOn of DAG node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.imrep_mass_and_support-a1.lusin_covector-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit 83274ea8a2c7). It is reused with its identical frozen Lean type, so it adds no DAG node. Used by the new child oriented_mass_lower (step 4: Lusin's theorem for L∘ξ' and the measure θ'·H^k⌞M' on the set W ∖ Z of finite measure), replacing step (3b) of the parent proof. The pinned Mathlib has no Lusin continuity theorem (only Lusin separation and Lusin–Souslin), so without this reuse the theorem would have to be re-proved. The reviewed proof from that node's parent-supplied handoff follows verbatim.

Source: step 4(a) of the parent proof, which cites Lusin's theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17). Lusin's continuity theorem is not in the pinned Mathlib, which has only the Lusin–Souslin and Lusin separation theorems. So the standard proof is given, in the compact, vector-valued form used by the parent.
Notation: Λ := Covector (Euclid P) n is a finite-dimensional real normed space, hence a separable metric space with a countable basis of open sets. Give Λ its Borel σ-algebra.
1. (Measurable modification.) Since f is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, there is a strongly measurable f' with f = f' μ-a.e. f' is a pointwise limit of simple functions with values in the metrizable space Λ, so it is Borel measurable. The set {f ≠ f'} is μ-null, so it lies in a measurable μ-null set Z (exists_measurable_superset_of_null). Put A₀ := A ∖ Z. Then A₀ ⊆ A is measurable, μ(A ∖ A₀) ≤ μ(Z) = 0, and f = f' on A₀.
2. (Inner regularity.) ν := μ.restrict A₀ is a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P, since ν(ℝ^P) = μ(A₀) ≤ μ(A) < ∞. ℝ^P is a Polish space, so ν is inner regular by compact sets (Ulam's theorem; in Mathlib, finite measures on completely metrizable second-countable spaces are InnerRegular, see MeasureTheory/Measure/RegularityCompacts.lean). Hence for every measurable B ⊆ A₀ and η > 0 there is a compact C ⊆ B with μ(B ∖ C) = ν(B ∖ C) < η.
3. (Compact pieces.) Let (O_k)_{k∈ℕ} be a countable basis of the topology of Λ, and S_k := f'^{-1}(O_k), which is measurable. By step 2 choose compact sets C_k ⊆ A₀ ∩ S_k and D_k ⊆ A₀ ∖ S_k with
 μ((A₀ ∩ S_k) ∖ C_k) < ε·2^{−k−3} and μ((A₀ ∖ S_k) ∖ D_k) < ε·2^{−k−3}.
 Let E_k := C_k ∪ D_k, a compact subset of A₀. Since A₀ ∖ E_k ⊆ ((A₀ ∩ S_k) ∖ C_k) ∪ ((A₀ ∖ S_k) ∖ D_k), μ(A₀ ∖ E_k) < ε·2^{−k−2}.
4. (The compact set.) K := ⋂_k E_k is closed and contained in the compact set E_0, so K is compact, and K ⊆ A₀ ⊆ A. As A ∖ K ⊆ (A ∖ A₀) ∪ ⋃_k (A₀ ∖ E_k), countable subadditivity gives μ(A ∖ K) ≤ 0 + Σ_k ε·2^{−k−2} = ε/2 < ε.
5. (Continuity.) Fix k.
 - If x ∈ K and f'(x) ∈ O_k, then x ∈ S_k, so x ∉ D_k because D_k ∩ S_k = ∅.
 - Conversely, if x ∈ K ∖ D_k, then x ∈ E_k ∖ D_k ⊆ C_k ⊆ S_k.
 Hence K ∩ f'^{-1}(O_k) = K ∖ D_k, which is relatively open in K because D_k is closed. Since (O_k) is a basis, the restriction f'|_K is continuous (IsTopologicalBasis.continuous_iff on the subtype K). As f = f' on K ⊆ A₀, f is continuous on K, i.e. ContinuousOn f K.
proof_key_steps: Replace f by a Borel modification f' and remove a measurable null set Z: A₀ = A ∖ Z.
μ restricted to A₀ is a finite Borel measure on the Polish space ℝ^P, hence inner regular by compact sets.
For a countable basis (O_k) of Λⁿ, choose compact C_k ⊆ A₀ ∩ f'^{-1}O_k and D_k ⊆ A₀ ∖ f'^{-1}O_k with defects < ε·2^{−k−3}.
K = ⋂_k (C_k ∪ D_k) is compact, K ⊆ A, and μ(A ∖ K) ≤ ε/2.
K ∩ f'^{-1}O_k = K ∖ D_k is relatively open in K, so f = f' is continuous on K.

subproblems.title: Smooth unit-norm approximation of a continuous covector field on a compact set
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (K V : Set (Euclid P)) (β : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n) (δ : ℝ), IsCompact K → IsOpen V → K ⊆ V → ContinuousOn β K → (∀ x ∈ K, covectorEuclideanNorm (β x) ≤ 1) → 0 < δ → ∃ ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n, IsTestForm ω ∧ tsupport ω ⊆ V ∧ (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (ω x) ≤ 1) ∧ ∀ x ∈ K, covectorEuclideanNorm (ω x - β x) ≤ δ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note. This child is the accepted declaration Submission.dor_ims_smooth_unit_approx of DAG node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.imrep_mass_and_support-a1.smooth_unit_approximation-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit 89e4c45cd3c1). It is reused with its identical frozen Lean type, so it adds no DAG node. Used by the new child oriented_mass_lower (step 5: one admissible smooth form δ-close to L∘ξ' on the Lusin compact set), replacing steps (3c)–(3e) of the parent proof (Tietze extension, normalization, mollification, cut-off), which this lemma packages. The reviewed proof from that node's parent-supplied handoff follows verbatim.

Source: steps 4(c)–(d) of the parent proof (Tietze extension, radial retraction onto the unit ball of |·|, cut-off, mollification). They are packaged so that only the estimate on K is recorded.
Notation: Λ := Covector (Euclid P) n with operator norm ‖·‖; |·| := covectorEuclideanNorm; 𝓘 is the set of strictly increasing I : Fin n → Fin P, and e_I := (e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}).
0. If K = ∅, then ω := 0 works: it is smooth with compact support, tsupport 0 = ∅ ⊆ V, and |0| = 0. Assume K ≠ ∅ from now on.
1. (The norm |·|.) Let 𝒜 : Λ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n → Fin P) be the linear map with 𝒜(α)_I := α(e_I) if I is strictly increasing and 0 otherwise. It is continuous (finite dimension), and by the definition of covectorEuclideanNorm, |α| = ‖𝒜(α)‖. Consequently:
 (N1) |·| is continuous;
 (N2) |cα| = |c|·|α|;
 (N3) |α + α'| ≤ |α| + |α'|;
 (N4) |∫ g dm| ≤ ∫ |g| dm for every finite measure m and m-integrable g : ℝ^P → Λ, since 𝒜 commutes with the Bochner integral and the norm of an integral is at most the integral of the norm;
 (N5) |α| ≤ C₀‖α‖ with C₀ := (#𝓘)^{1/2}, because |α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_k ‖e_{I(k)}‖ = ‖α‖.
2. (Tietze.) K is closed and β|_K is continuous. Λ is a finite-dimensional real vector space, so the Tietze extension theorem gives a continuous β̃ : ℝ^P → Λ with β̃ = β on K (Mathlib ContinuousMap.exists_restrict_eq with the TietzeExtension instance RCLike.instTietzeExtensionTVS for finite-dimensional real spaces, or coordinatewise in a basis).
3. (Retraction.) Put ρ(α) := max(1, |α|)^{−1}·α. ρ is continuous by (N1). By (N2), |ρ(α)| = |α|/max(1, |α|) ≤ 1, and ρ(α) = α when |α| ≤ 1.
4. (Cut-off.) K is compact and V open, so there is r > 0 with cthickening(2r, K) := {x : dist(x, K) ≤ 2r} ⊆ V (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). Put χ(x) := max(0, 1 − dist(x, K)/r). χ is continuous, 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1 and χ = 1 on K. Since χ(x) = 0 when dist(x, K) ≥ r, support χ ⊆ thickening(r, K) := {x : dist(x, K) < r}.
5. (Continuous unit field.) g := χ·(ρ ∘ β̃) is continuous, with support g ⊆ thickening(r, K) and tsupport g ⊆ cthickening(r, K), which is compact (K compact, ℝ^P proper). Moreover |g(x)| = χ(x)·|ρ(β̃(x))| ≤ 1 for all x. For x ∈ K, g(x) = ρ(β(x)) = β(x), because χ = 1 and |β| ≤ 1 there.
6. (Mollification.) g is continuous with compact support, hence uniformly continuous. Choose s with 0 < s ≤ r such that ‖g(y) − g(x)‖ ≤ δ/(C₀ + 1) whenever dist(y, x) < s. Let φ ≥ 0 be a smooth bump function with ∫ φ dx = 1 and support φ = B_s(0) (Mathlib ContDiffBump (0 : ℝ^P) with rOut = s, normed for Lebesgue measure). Define ω := φ ⋆ g, ω(x) = ∫ φ(t)·g(x − t) dt (Bochner integral in Λ).
 (i) ω is C^∞: it is the convolution of a C^∞ compactly supported kernel with a continuous, hence locally integrable, function (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left).
 (ii) support ω ⊆ support φ + support g ⊆ B_s(0) + thickening(r, K) ⊆ thickening(2r, K), using s ≤ r (support_convolution_subset). Hence tsupport ω ⊆ cthickening(2r, K) ⊆ V, a compact set. So ω is C^∞ with compact support (IsTestForm ω) and tsupport ω ⊆ V.
 (iii) For every x, by (N4), φ ≥ 0, |g| ≤ 1 and ∫ φ = 1: |ω(x)| ≤ ∫ φ(t)·|g(x − t)| dt ≤ ∫ φ(t) dt = 1.
 (iv) For every x, φ(t) = 0 unless |t| < s, and ∫ φ = 1. So ‖ω(x) − g(x)‖ = ‖∫ φ(t)·(g(x − t) − g(x)) dt‖ ≤ δ/(C₀ + 1) (ContDiffBump.dist_normed_convolution_le). By (N5), |ω(x) − g(x)| ≤ C₀·δ/(C₀ + 1) ≤ δ.
7. For x ∈ K, g(x) = β(x) by step 5, so |ω(x) − β(x)| ≤ δ by 6(iv). Together with 6(i)–(iii), ω has all the required properties.
proof_key_steps: |·| = ‖𝒜(·)‖ for the coefficient map 𝒜, so |·| is a continuous norm with |∫ g| ≤ ∫ |g| and |α| ≤ C₀‖α‖.
Extend β|_K continuously (Tietze), retract radially onto {|·| ≤ 1}, and multiply by the cut-off χ = max(0, 1 − dist(·, K)/r): g is continuous, |g| ≤ 1, g = β on K, tsupport g ⊆ cthickening(r, K).
Mollify with a normalized smooth bump of radius s ≤ r: the result is C^∞ with tsupport ⊆ cthickening(2r, K) ⊆ V and |ω| ≤ 1 by convexity.
Uniform continuity gives |ω − g| ≤ δ everywhere, and g = β on K.

subproblems.title: Upper mass bound for a current given on V by an oriented weighted set (Simon 6.2.5, 6.3.2(3), '≤')
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, U, V, M' ⊆ ℝ^P (Euclid P), T ∈ 𝒟_k(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U k), θ' : ℝ^P → ℝ and ξ' : ℝ^P → Λ_k(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P k). Assume: θ'(x) ≥ 0 for every x; for H^k⌞M'-a.e. x (H^k = μHE[k]) there is a linear subspace Q of ℝ^P with IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ'(x)) Q (ξ'(x)(α) = ±α(τ_1, …, τ_k) for an orthonormal basis τ of Q); and T(ω) = ∫_{M'} θ'(x)·ξ'(x)(ω(x)) dH^k(x) (Bochner integral for H^k⌞M') for every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ V. Then for every Borel (measurable) set W ⊆ V: M_W(T) ≤ ∫⁻_{M'∩W} ofReal(θ'(x)) dH^k(x) in [0, ∞]. Here M_W(T) = T.massOn W is the supremum of ofReal(T(ω)) over ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and Euclidean coefficient norm |ω(x)| = covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for every x. No measurability of θ' or ξ' and no openness of V or W is assumed.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U V M' : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U k) (θ' : Euclid P → ℝ) (ξ' : Euclid P → MultiVector P k), (∀ x, 0 ≤ θ' x) → (∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[k].restrict M'), ∃ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ' x) Q) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U k, tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) ⊆ V → T ω = ∫ x in M', θ' x * ξ' x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μHE[k]) → ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet W → W ⊆ V → T.massOn W ≤ ∫⁻ x in M' ∩ W, ENNReal.ofReal (θ' x) ∂μHE[k]
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Simon Ch. 6, 2.5 (the mass M_W(T), chapter-06.txt lines 224–240) and 3.2(3) (M_W(T) = ∫_{M∩W} θ dH^n for T = τ(M, θ, ξ), chapter-06.txt lines 755–770). This is the upper half of the parent proof: its step 1 (1a) and step 2, specialized to a measurable W ⊆ V. Two simplifications relative to the parent's step 2: no case distinction on whether I(W) is finite is needed, and no measurability of θ' or ξ' is used, because the estimate goes through the inequality |∫ g| ≤ ∫⁻ |g|, which holds for every function g (step 5).

Sibling child used (an accepted declaration, reused with its identical frozen type):
- unit_orientation_dual (Submission.dor_ims_unitOrientation_dual), part (a) only: if ξ ∈ Λ_k(ℝ^P) is a unit orientation of some subspace Q (IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q), then |ξ(α)| ≤ |α| for every k-covector α.

Notation.
- H^k := μHE[k] and μ := H^k⌞M' (μHE[k].restrict M'). For α ∈ Λ^k := Covector (Euclid P) k, |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α.
- ∫ g dμ is the Bochner integral, as in the frozen statement; by definition it is 0 when g is not μ-integrable.
- I(W) := ∫⁻_{M'∩W} ofReal(θ') dH^k ∈ [0, ∞].
- ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) is admissible for M_W(T) if tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for every x. M_W(T) = T.massOn W is the supremum of ofReal(T(ω)) over admissible ω.

Proof. Fix the data and hypotheses of the statement and a measurable set W ⊆ V.

1. (Pointwise duality bound.) Call x good if |ξ'(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every α ∈ Λ^k. By hypothesis, for μ-a.e. x there is a subspace Q with IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ'(x)) Q, and then x is good by unit_orientation_dual (a). Hence μ-a.e. x is good.

2. (Reduction to one admissible form.) M_W(T) is the supremum of ofReal(T(ω)) over admissible ω, so it suffices to prove ofReal(T(ω)) ≤ I(W) for every admissible ω. Fix one.

3. (Representation.) tsupport ω ⊆ W ⊆ V, so the representation hypothesis gives T(ω) = ∫ g dμ with g(x) := θ'(x)·ξ'(x)(ω(x)).

4. (Domination.) For every good x, |g(x)| ≤ 1_W(x)·θ'(x):
 - if x ∉ W, then x ∉ tsupport ω because tsupport ω ⊆ W; a function vanishes outside its topological support, so ω(x) = 0, hence ξ'(x)(ω(x)) = 0 by linearity of ξ'(x), and g(x) = 0;
 - if x ∈ W, then, since θ'(x) ≥ 0, |g(x)| = θ'(x)·|ξ'(x)(ω(x))| ≤ θ'(x)·|ω(x)| ≤ θ'(x), by step 1 and |ω(x)| ≤ 1.
 By step 1, ofReal|g(x)| ≤ 1_W(x)·ofReal(θ'(x)) for μ-a.e. x.

5. (Estimate.) In [0, ∞],
 ofReal(T(ω)) ≤ ofReal|T(ω)| = ofReal|∫ g dμ| ≤ ∫⁻ ofReal|g| dμ.
 The last inequality is the triangle inequality ofReal|∫ g dμ| ≤ ofReal(∫ |g| dμ) = ∫⁻ ofReal|g| dμ when g is μ-integrable, and it is trivial when g is not μ-integrable, since then ∫ g dμ = 0 (in Mathlib: enorm_integral_le_lintegral_enorm, valid for every g). By step 4 and monotonicity of the lower Lebesgue integral under a.e. inequalities,
 ∫⁻ ofReal|g| dμ ≤ ∫⁻ 1_W·ofReal(θ') dμ = ∫⁻_W ofReal(θ') dμ = ∫⁻ ofReal(θ') d(H^k⌞(W ∩ M')) = I(W).
 Here W is measurable: the integral of 1_W·f is the integral of f over W (lintegral_indicator), (H^k⌞M')⌞W = H^k⌞(W ∩ M') (Measure.restrict_restrict), and W ∩ M' = M' ∩ W. Hence ofReal(T(ω)) ≤ I(W).

6. (Conclusion.) Taking the supremum over all admissible ω gives M_W(T) ≤ I(W). ∎
proof_key_steps: unit_orientation_dual (a): |ξ'(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every α at H^k⌞M'-a.e. x.
For admissible ω (tsupport ω ⊆ W ⊆ V, |ω| ≤ 1): T(ω) = ∫_{M'} g with g = θ'·ξ'(ω), and |g| ≤ 1_W·θ' a.e. on M' because ω = 0 off W.
ofReal T(ω) ≤ ofReal|∫ g| ≤ ∫⁻ ofReal|g| ≤ ∫⁻_{M'} 1_W·ofReal θ' = I(W) for measurable W; take the supremum over admissible ω.

subproblems.title: Lower mass bound for a current given on V by an oriented weighted set (Simon 6.2.5, 6.3.2(3), '≥')
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, U, V, M' ⊆ ℝ^P (Euclid P), T ∈ 𝒟_k(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U k), θ' : ℝ^P → ℝ and ξ' : ℝ^P → Λ_k(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P k). Assume: V ⊆ U; θ' is Borel measurable with θ'(x) ≥ 0 for every x; ξ' is a.e. strongly measurable for H^k⌞M' (H^k = μHE[k]; M' is an arbitrary set and H^k⌞M' is the restriction of H^k to M'); for H^k⌞M'-a.e. x there is a linear subspace Q of ℝ^P with IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ'(x)) Q (ξ'(x)(α) = ±α(τ_1, …, τ_k) for an orthonormal basis τ of Q); and T(ω) = ∫_{M'} θ'(x)·ξ'(x)(ω(x)) dH^k(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ V. Then for every open W ⊆ V with I(W) := ∫⁻_{M'∩W} ofReal(θ'(x)) dH^k(x) < ∞ we have I(W) ≤ M_W(T) in [0, ∞]. Here M_W(T) = T.massOn W is the supremum of ofReal(T(ω)) over ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and Euclidean coefficient norm |ω(x)| = covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for every x.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U V M' : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U k) (θ' : Euclid P → ℝ) (ξ' : Euclid P → MultiVector P k), V ⊆ U → Measurable θ' → (∀ x, 0 ≤ θ' x) → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ' (μHE[k].restrict M') → (∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[k].restrict M'), ∃ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ' x) Q) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U k, tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) ⊆ V → T ω = ∫ x in M', θ' x * ξ' x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μHE[k]) → ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → W ⊆ V → ∫⁻ x in M' ∩ W, ENNReal.ofReal (θ' x) ∂μHE[k] ≠ ∞ → ∫⁻ x in M' ∩ W, ENNReal.ofReal (θ' x) ∂μHE[k] ≤ T.massOn W
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Simon Ch. 6, 2.5 (the mass M_W(T), chapter-06.txt lines 224–240) and 3.2(3) (M_W(T) = ∫_{M∩W} θ dH^n, chapter-06.txt lines 755–770). This is the lower half of the parent proof: its step 1 and step 3. Steps (3a)–(3b) of the parent (the measure ν = θ'·H^k⌞M', finite on W, and Lusin's theorem) are carried out with the accepted lemma lusin_covector. Steps (3c)–(3e) (Tietze extension, normalization to |·| ≤ 1, mollification, smooth cut-off) are exactly what the accepted lemma smooth_unit_approximation packages: for each δ > 0 it gives one admissible form that is δ-close to L∘ξ' on the Lusin set K. Because that form is δ-close on K, rather than a member of a pointwise convergent sequence, the parent's dominated-convergence passage (3f) is not needed. The parent's estimate (3g) is applied directly to T(ω), with the one extra error term δ·ν(K) (step 8). Measurability of M' (a hypothesis of the parent) is not needed and not assumed: every restriction below is to one of the Borel sets W, Z, A, K, and (H^k⌞M')⌞B = H^k⌞(B ∩ M') for Borel B and an arbitrary set M'.

Sibling children used (accepted declarations, reused with their identical frozen types):
- unit_orientation_dual (Submission.dor_ims_unitOrientation_dual): there is a continuous linear map L : Λ_k(ℝ^P) → Λ^k(ℝ^P) such that whenever IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q: (a) |ξ(α)| ≤ |α| for every k-covector α; (b) |L(ξ)| ≤ 1; (c) ξ(L(ξ)) = 1.
- lusin_covector (Submission.dor_ims_lusin_continuousOn): for a measure ν on ℝ^P, a measurable A ⊆ ℝ^P with ν(A) < ∞, a ν-a.e. strongly measurable f : ℝ^P → Λ^k(ℝ^P) and a real η > 0, there is a compact K ⊆ A with ν(A ∖ K) < η such that f is continuous on K.
- smooth_unit_approximation (Submission.dor_ims_smooth_unit_approx): for K ⊆ G ⊆ ℝ^P with K compact and G open, β : ℝ^P → Λ^k(ℝ^P) continuous on K with |β(x)| ≤ 1 for x ∈ K, and δ > 0, there is a smooth compactly supported k-form ω₀ (IsTestForm ω₀) with tsupport ω₀ ⊆ G, |ω₀(x)| ≤ 1 for every x and |ω₀(x) − β(x)| ≤ δ for every x ∈ K.

Notation.
- H^k := μHE[k]; μ := H^k⌞M'; Λ^k := Covector (Euclid P) k with |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; Λ_k := MultiVector P k.
- ν := μ with density ofReal∘θ', i.e. ν(B) = ∫⁻_B ofReal(θ') dμ = ∫⁻_{M'∩B} ofReal(θ') dH^k for Borel B (the second equality because (H^k⌞M')⌞B = H^k⌞(B ∩ M') for Borel B).
- I := I(W) = ∫⁻_{M'∩W} ofReal(θ') dH^k, assumed finite.
- ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) is admissible for M_W(T) if tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for every x; by definition of the supremum, ofReal(T(ω)) ≤ M_W(T) for each admissible ω.

Proof. Fix the data and hypotheses of the statement and an open W ⊆ V with I < ∞.

1. (Good points.) Let L be the map of unit_orientation_dual for (P, k). Call x good if (a) |ξ'(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every α ∈ Λ^k, (b) |L(ξ'(x))| ≤ 1 and (c) ξ'(x)(L(ξ'(x))) = 1. By the orientation hypothesis and unit_orientation_dual, μ-a.e. x is good. So the set of points that are not good is μ-null, and it is contained in a Borel set Z with μ(Z) = 0 (every null set has a measurable null superset).

2. (The measure ν.) ν ≪ μ, since ν(B) = ∫⁻_B ofReal(θ') dμ = 0 whenever μ(B) = 0. Hence ν(Z) = 0, and ν-a.e. x is good. W is open, hence Borel, so ν(W) = ∫⁻_W ofReal(θ') d(H^k⌞M') = ∫⁻_{M'∩W} ofReal(θ') dH^k = I < ∞, and ν(B) ≤ I for every Borel B ⊆ W. Write m := I, a real number ≥ 0.
 Density formula: ofReal∘θ' is measurable (θ' is) and finite everywhere, so every ν-integrable g : ℝ^P → ℝ satisfies ∫ g dν = ∫ (ofReal θ'(x)).toReal·g(x) dμ(x) = ∫ θ'·g dμ, because (ofReal θ'(x)).toReal = θ'(x) when θ'(x) ≥ 0 (Mathlib: integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul).

3. (Reduction.) It suffices to prove r ≤ M_W(T) for every real r ≥ 0 with r < I; then I ≤ M_W(T) in [0, ∞]. Fix such an r, choose ε > 0 with r + ε < I, and put η := ε/4 > 0, so that r + 4η < m.

4. (Lusin.) h := L∘ξ' : ℝ^P → Λ^k is ν-a.e. strongly measurable: ξ' is μ-a.e. strongly measurable by hypothesis, hence ν-a.e. strongly measurable because ν ≪ μ, and L is continuous. The set A := W ∖ Z is Borel with ν(A) ≤ ν(W) < ∞. By lusin_covector, applied to ν, A, h and η, there is a compact K ⊆ A with ν(A ∖ K) < η such that h is continuous on K.
 (4a) K ⊆ W and K ∩ Z = ∅, so every x ∈ K is good; in particular |h(x)| ≤ 1 for x ∈ K, by (b).
 (4b) W ∖ K ⊆ (A ∖ K) ∪ Z, so ν(W ∖ K) ≤ ν(A ∖ K) + ν(Z) < η.
 (4c) K is compact, hence Borel, and K ⊆ W, so ν(K) + ν(W ∖ K) = ν(W) = m, all terms finite. With (4b), ν(K) > m − η; also ν(K) ≤ m.

5. (An admissible form.) Put δ := η/(m + 1) > 0. Apply smooth_unit_approximation to the compact set K, the open set G := W ⊇ K, β := h (continuous on K, with |β| ≤ 1 on K by (4a)) and δ. It gives a smooth compactly supported k-form ω₀ with tsupport ω₀ ⊆ W, |ω₀(x)| ≤ 1 for every x, and |ω₀(x) − h(x)| ≤ δ for every x ∈ K. Since tsupport ω₀ ⊆ W ⊆ V ⊆ U, ω₀ is an element ω of 𝒟^k(U), and ω is admissible for M_W(T). Hence ofReal(T(ω)) ≤ M_W(T).

6. (Integrability and the value of T(ω).) Let f(x) := ξ'(x)(ω₀(x)).
 - f is ν-a.e. strongly measurable: it is the composite of x ↦ (ξ'(x), ω₀(x)), which is ν-a.e. strongly measurable (ξ' by step 4, ω₀ continuous), with the evaluation pairing Λ_k × Λ^k → ℝ, (ζ, α) ↦ ζ(α), which is continuous (a bounded bilinear map).
 - For every good x, |f(x)| ≤ 1_W(x): if x ∉ W then x ∉ tsupport ω₀, so ω₀(x) = 0 and f(x) = 0; if x ∈ W then |f(x)| ≤ |ω₀(x)| ≤ 1 by (a).
 - 1_W is ν-integrable because ν(W) < ∞. Hence f is ν-integrable, and, by the representation hypothesis (tsupport ω ⊆ W ⊆ V) and the density formula of step 2,
 T(ω) = ∫_{M'} θ'(x)·ξ'(x)(ω₀(x)) dH^k(x) = ∫ θ'·f dμ = ∫ f dν.

7. (Pointwise lower bound.) For every good x,
 f(x) ≥ (1 − δ)·1_K(x) − 1_{W∖K}(x).
 - x ∈ K: by linearity of ξ'(x) and (c), f(x) = ξ'(x)(h(x)) + ξ'(x)(ω₀(x) − h(x)) = 1 + ξ'(x)(ω₀(x) − h(x)) ≥ 1 − |ω₀(x) − h(x)| ≥ 1 − δ, using (a).
 - x ∈ W ∖ K: f(x) ≥ −|ξ'(x)(ω₀(x))| ≥ −|ω₀(x)| ≥ −1, by (a).
 - x ∉ W: ω₀(x) = 0, so f(x) = 0, which is the value of the right side.
 Since ν-a.e. x is good, the inequality holds ν-a.e.

8. (Integration and arithmetic.) The right side of step 7 is ν-integrable (ν(K) and ν(W ∖ K) are finite), so monotonicity of the integral gives
 T(ω) = ∫ f dν ≥ (1 − δ)·ν(K) − ν(W ∖ K) = ν(K) − δ·ν(K) − ν(W ∖ K).
 Now δ·ν(K) ≤ δ·m = η·m/(m + 1) < η, ν(W ∖ K) < η by (4b), and ν(K) > m − η by (4c). Therefore
 T(ω) > (m − η) − η − η = m − 3η > (r + 4η) − 3η = r + η > r.

9. (Conclusion.) By steps 5 and 8, r = ofReal(r) ≤ ofReal(T(ω)) ≤ M_W(T). Since r ∈ [0, I) was arbitrary, I ≤ M_W(T). ∎
proof_key_steps: unit_orientation_dual gives L with |ξ'(α)| ≤ |α|, |L(ξ')| ≤ 1 and ξ'(L(ξ')) = 1 off a Borel H^k⌞M'-null set Z; ν := θ'·H^k⌞M' satisfies ν ≪ H^k⌞M' and ν(W) = I < ∞.
Reduce to r < I; with η = ε/4 and r + 4η < I, lusin_covector on A = W ∖ Z gives a compact K ⊆ A with ν(A ∖ K) < η on which L∘ξ' is continuous; since ν(Z) = 0, ν(W ∖ K) < η.
smooth_unit_approximation gives an admissible ω with tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω| ≤ 1 and |ω − L∘ξ'| ≤ δ := η/(I + 1) on K.
T(ω) = ∫ ξ'(ω) dν ≥ (1 − δ)ν(K) − ν(W ∖ K) > I − 3η > r, so r ≤ M_W(T); hence I ≤ M_W(T).
